source: Chi, Feltovich, Glaser (1981) Categorization and representation of physics problems by experts and novices
finding: Card-sorting study. Physics PhD students sorted mechanics problems by principle (energy conservation, Newton's second law). Undergraduates sorted by surface objects (inclined planes, springs, pulleys).
numbers: Experiment 1: 8 advanced physics PhD students vs 8 undergraduates with one mechanics course, 24 textbook problems (recalled; check). Experts' groups mostly matched solution principle; novices' mostly matched literal objects.
limits: From memory; not opened this session (publisher site blocked by Cloudflare 403, search quota used up). Verify numbers before use.
agent_relevance: Core claim for S2: a good representation is keyed to the governing principle, not the story objects.

source: Chi, Feltovich, Glaser (1981) Experiments 2-4 (problem summaries, similarity ratings, hierarchy)
finding: Experts asked to summarise problems state the principle and the conditions for applying it. Novices state the objects and given quantities. Expert knowledge is organised as schemas with the principle on top and applicability conditions beneath.
numbers: Details of N and ratings not verified.
limits: From memory; not opened this session (publisher site blocked by Cloudflare 403, search quota used up). Verify numbers before use.
agent_relevance: The expert representation includes WHEN a principle applies, not only its name. An S2 restatement should list applicability conditions.

source: Kortemeyer (2025) The Boiling-Frog Problem of Physics Education
finding: Direct LLM run of the Chi paradigm. GPT-5 Thinking sorted 60 exam items by solution similarity. Clusters were topic-oriented and solution-relevant, not surface-driven. Author: the outcome is not novice-like.
numbers: 60 multiple-choice items from two comprehensive finals (Fall 2008, Spring 2009), uploaded in one batch; one run; coded by the author. Same model scored 27/30 and 25/30 on those exams and 24/26 (92.3%) on TUG-Kv4.0.
quote: valid categories are neither surface-level ... nor so abstract as to collapse distinctions
limits: Single model, single run, no human control in the same paper, author-coded; original Chi card set unavailable. Author calls the paradigm notoriously difficult to replicate (cites Wolf et al.).
agent_relevance: Frontier reasoning models already group by solution method. The gap is not seeing deep structure in clean textbook problems; test on messy or disguised problems.

source: Kortemeyer (2025) novice-prompting result
finding: Prompts meant to elicit novice-like behaviour changed the tone of GPT-5 Thinking, not its method, on a classic elevator problem. The model worked symbolically and verified results.
numbers: Single worked problem; qualitative.
limits: Qualitative single-problem observation.
agent_relevance: A strong model cannot easily be made to hold a surface representation. Look for surface failures in adversarial items instead.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in Large Language Models
finding: Step-Back prompting makes the model first state the principle or concept behind a question, then solve with it. An engineered principle-first step.
numbers: PaLM-2L MMLU Physics 66.4% base, 65% CoT, 73.2% Step-Back; Chemistry 70.9%, 75.3%, 81.8%. GPT-4 Physics 69.4%, +CoT 82.9%. Abstract: +7%, +11% (MMLU phys, chem), +27% TimeQA, +7% MuSiQue. Corrects 20.5% of baseline errors but introduces 11.9% on Physics.
quote: Reasoning step is still the bottleneck
limits: Gains are small or absent when the base model is strong (GPT-4 CoT rivals it on Physics). Most remaining errors are reasoning errors, not abstraction errors.
agent_relevance: Closest engineered analogue of the expert principle-first representation. Helps weaker models. Costs 11.9% new errors, so gate it rather than always run (G1).

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Step-Back error analysis
finding: On MMLU high-school physics the largest class of remaining Step-Back errors is the reasoning step, even when first principles are retrieved correctly.
numbers: Five error classes annotated over all wrong predictions; Reasoning dominates (figure; counts not read).
quote: even if the first principles are retrieved correctly, deep reasoning and math are involved
limits: Counts are in a figure.
agent_relevance: Naming the right principle does not finish the job. Pair S2 with a checked solve step.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: Analogical prompting has the model recall relevant solved problems and the knowledge behind them, then solve. It outperforms 0-shot and manual few-shot CoT.
numbers: Average accuracy gain +4% on GSM8K, MATH, Codeforces and BIG-Bench with several base LLMs.
limits: Average gain only; self-generated exemplars can be wrong.
agent_relevance: Self-generated similar problems index by structure, the expert move in Chi. Candidate S2 operator; verify exemplars with code.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning
finding: Decomposing a problem into ordered subproblems lets a model solve harder problems than the examples. A structural re-description step.
numbers: Abstract: code-davinci-002 reaches 99% or more on SCAN splits including length with 14 exemplars, vs 16% with chain-of-thought.
limits: Decomposition is one kind of representation; per-split numbers not copied.
agent_relevance: Representation as decomposition can transform results on compositional tasks.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: Adding one irrelevant sentence to a grade-school math problem sharply lowers accuracy. A surface-capture failure, novice-like.
numbers: Performance on GSM-IC greatly decreases vs GSM8K (exact drop not extracted). Mitigations: self-consistency, exemplars containing irrelevant context, the instruction to ignore irrelevant information.
limits: 2022-era models (code-davinci-002, PaLM).
agent_relevance: Quantifies surface capture; the S2 restate step should drop given-but-unused facts.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic
finding: Changing only names or numbers in GSM8K templates lowers accuracy and raises variance. Adding one seemingly relevant but unneeded clause (GSM-NoOp) drops accuracy up to 65%.
numbers: Drops up to 65% across all state-of-the-art models on NoOp; accuracy falls as clause count rises; best-to-worst instantiation gap over 12% for some models.
quote: even though the added clause does not contribute to the reasoning chain
limits: Authors' interpretation (pattern replication, not reasoning) is contested; later reasoning models may drop less (not verified).
agent_relevance: Strong LLM evidence of surface-keyed representation under distractors. Test any S2 design on NoOp-style variants.

source: Lewis, Mitchell (2024) Using Counterfactual Tasks to Evaluate the Generality of Analogical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Letter-string analogies with permuted or symbol alphabets: humans stay high, GPT-3, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 fall sharply. Structure is partly bound to familiar surface content.
numbers: Humans (46 samples in their data) vs three GPT models; models decline on counterfactual alphabets; a comprehension check shows models often still understand the new ordering.
limits: Text-only letter strings; models of early 2024; later reasoning models not tested.
agent_relevance: Counterfactual relabelling is a test for S2: if the answer changes when surface changes, representation was shallow.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) matched or exceeded humans in zero-shot digit matrices, letter-string, four-term verbal and story analogies; GPT-4 preliminary better.
numbers: Digit Matrices: human N=40, OR=1.88, p=0.005, 95% CI [1.21, 2.91]; letter-string N=57; verbal analogies N=57; story analogies N=54 (human samples).
limits: Lewis and Mitchell show failure on counterfactual variants. Possible training-data overlap.
agent_relevance: Positive side of the same question: structure mapping exists on familiar formats.

source: Lampinen et al. (2024) Language models show human-like content effects on reasoning tasks
finding: LLMs, like humans, reason better when content is believable and fits prior beliefs. The same logical form performs differently with realistic vs arbitrary content.
numbers: Natural language inference, syllogisms and the Wason selection task; Chinchilla among models; accuracy lower on arbitrary Wason.
limits: Different phenomenon from card-sorting, same cause: content contaminates structure.
agent_relevance: Expect representation to shift with content; restating in abstract symbols is a check.
